claim: Studying worked examples beats solving equivalent problems for novices in maths: pooled g=0.48 (43 articles, 55 studies, 181 effects); founding work is Sweller and Cooper 1985 (not opened).
agent_test: Arm A solves cold; arm B gets one solved case of the same type. Equal tokens by trimming B's reasoning budget by the example length.
audit_note: Numbers match (ERIC abstract: 43 articles, 55 studies, 181 effects, g=0.48); the Springer pages were paywalled so Sweller 2019 was verified only by Crossref metadata, and the meta-analysis covers elementary to postsecondary learners, not novices specifically (the evidence lists the author as Booth; actual authors are Barbieri, Miller-Cotto, Clerjuste, Chawla).

claim: The effect is strongest for multi-step, high element-interactivity procedures; low-interactivity material (definitions) shows a reverse effect. In LLM chain-of-thought the gain also grows with step count and is tiny on the easiest sets.
agent_test: Split a benchmark by gold step count; compare example-first gain per bin.
audit_note: Sweller 2019 full text was paywalled and not opened; the LLM half (Wei, Fu, Zhou) was verified.

claim: Expertise reversal: as learner knowledge rises the example advantage shrinks or reverses, so guidance should fade. The Kalyuga papers were not opened and the LLM evidence is a persona simulation. Gap search: for LLMs, modern instruction-tuned models gain nothing from exemplars beyond format (Cheng 2026), R1 reports few-shot hurts, and note injection helps items the model mostly fails but hurts solved items (Notes to Self 2026).
agent_test: Show the full example on a type until code-checked success, then offer blank-step completion; compare with always-full.

claim: Fading (completion problems) improves near transfer over example-problem pairs; far transfer is unreliable and one 2024 trial found no fading advantage.
agent_test: Same as K03, but test on a new problem type as well as the same type.

claim: Self-explanation prompts do not add to worked examples in the maths meta-analysis (negative moderator), though they helped conceptual translation tasks in one small study and open-ended LLM-supported explanation helped transfer explanation quality.
agent_test: Add or drop an 'explain each step' instruction on top of examples at equal tokens; check whether explanation tokens return more than they cost.

claim: Correct examples beat incorrect or mixed sets in maths; in LLM prompts, random step errors cost little but systematic errors in every example drive accuracy toward zero.
agent_test: Inject wrong steps into 1 of 3 library examples and measure the drop; verify library entries by code before storage.
audit_note: Minor: Zhou's error-injection result is on an addition algorithmic task only.

claim: For LLMs, relevance to the query and coherent step order matter more than the validity of the example's reasoning; irrelevant exemplars fall below the no-example baseline (GSM8K 11.0 vs 15.4).
agent_test: Retrieval ablation: relevant vs shuffled-order vs irrelevant exemplar on a fixed item set.
audit_note: Minor: the 11.0 vs 15.4 result is one model (text-davinci-002) on GSM8K.

claim: Part of what in-context examples do for a model is set format, label space and input distribution, not teach correctness (random labels cost 0-5 points on classification). Evidence is classification only.
agent_test: Replace final answers in maths examples with wrong ones; compare to wrong steps.

claim: Skill-matched example choice beats topic-matched and complex CoT on MATH (GPT-4 53.88 vs 50.31/50.30, CoT 42.2); the gain nearly vanishes on near-ceiling GSM8K (93.00 to 94.31) and is larger for weaker models.
agent_test: Tag a held-out set by skill; compare skill-matched, topic-matched and random library retrieval at equal prompt length.

claim: In one study (Chen et al. 2024, ChatGPT, dynamic programming task), putting skill definitions and worked examples that cite those skills in one prompt gave 98.0 vs 72.0 for CoT; grounding the steps in skills mattered most (82.0 without grounding) while dropping the skill text cost only 4 points (94.0).
agent_test: Ablate skill text and skill grounding in the library entry format.
audit_note: Numbers match Chen et al. (SKiC), but removing the skill text costs only 4 points (98.0 to 94.0) versus 16 for removing grounding (82.0), so 'both parts are needed' is too strong; the claim also rests on one paper, with the second listed paper (subgoal theorem proving) not testing it.
claim_before_audit: Skill definitions plus worked examples that cite those skills in one prompt generalise to harder items; both parts are needed (DP 98.0 vs CoT 72.0; no skill text 94.0; no grounding 82.0).

claim: Explicit, unambiguous step-by-step examples teach an algorithm in context and generalise to longer inputs (addition length 19: 90.5% vs 9.5%).
agent_test: Write the subgoal procedure as explicit steps; test on instances longer than the examples.

claim: Choosing longer, more complex examples beats random, centroid and handcrafted sets (GSM8K Codex 66.6 vs 61.0; davinci-002 55.4 vs 48.1), mainly on items needing more steps.
agent_test: Select library entries by step count vs random; report gain by item difficulty.

claim: Similarity retrieval wins mainly where test items nearly duplicate library items (MathQA 69.5 vs 42.5); structure-based retrieval beats wording-based, most for small models; similarity-picked demos propagate the same mistake (unresolved errors 46.9% vs 25.8%).
agent_test: Report the near-duplicate rate; compare surface vs structure retrieval on a deduplicated set.
audit_note: Claim numbers match; the evidence line for Yang et al. mislabels table rows (18.6/27.6/34.3 are different rows, not random/semantic/graph for one model) but the paper does state the graph retrieval gain is larger for smaller models.

claim: Showing the decomposition into subproblems in the demo gives large gains on length generalisation (SCAN 99.7 vs about 16) and small ones on GSM8K, rising with step count (5+ steps 45.23 vs 39.07; at 2 steps CoT is better).
agent_test: Compare examples with explicit subgoal lists vs flat chains at 2-step and 5+-step items.

claim: Subgoal-labelled worked examples beat unlabelled ones in programming courses (N=307; quizzes medium effect, exams small); effect depended on arrangement across three pooled studies. Only talk slides and abstracts seen. LLM analogue with a verifier: subgoal-based demos 45.5 vs 38.9 miniF2F-test (Isabelle), subgoal ablation about +5 points.
agent_test: Label subgoals in library entries vs unlabelled; test on far transfer.

claim: Letting the model write its own relevant exemplars helps on large models (GSM8K 75.0 to 77.8; PaLM2 60.8 to 81.7) but loses to retrieved labelled examples on small ones; a second study found relevance did not matter while correctness did. Gap search: self-made examples fail when wrong chains are retrieved by similarity (Auto-CoT: 21.3% zero-shot errors on MultiArith) and work when filtered by a verifier (STaR); no direct test fixes correctness and varies self vs retrieved.
agent_test: Self-generated vs retrieved vs none, with a correctness check on the generated exemplar.

claim: Self-generation helps when the example is created and solved in the same turn; reusing it as a plain demo gives almost nothing (GPT-4o GSM8K 54.59 integrated vs 50.49 decoupled, zero-shot 49.89). Not re-verified.
agent_test: Integrated vs decoupled arms at equal tokens.

claim: A single demo can hurt: one-shot failed on 1.83 to 34.96% of problems solved zero-shot; a rejection rule falling back to zero-shot helps.
agent_test: Run with and without a fall-back to no-example when retrieval similarity is low.

claim: Experience-note libraries are model-dependent: Llama-3.2-3B 43.11 to 46.42, Qwen-1.5B 50.23 to 49.14, Gemma lost; buffer-of-thought templates helped GPT-4 on Game of 24 (11.0 CoT to 82.4). Not re-verified. Numbers for Notes to Self re-opened and confirmed (gap search); Gemma loses accuracy even with a blank template.
agent_test: Test the library on at least 3 models; keep it only where a check shows gain.

claim: LLM-authored worked solutions and hints are often flawed: in Pardos and Bhandari (v1, N=77) 70% of ChatGPT hints passed manual quality checks, and only the human-hint groups showed a significant pre-to-post gain (ChatGPT groups started with higher pre-test scores); in Gupta et al. 2025 only 56.6% of 150 LLM tutoring dialogs were fully correct, though 90% were rated high quality.
agent_test: Code-verify every generated library entry before admission; log the rejection rate.
audit_note: Numbers match (70% of ChatGPT hints passed checks; human-hint groups significant pre-post gain, ChatGPT groups not in v1; 56.6% of 150 tutoring dialogs fully correct), but neither study measures the quality of human-authored solutions, so 'less reliable than human ones' is not shown for quality; the ChatGPT groups also began with much higher pre-test scores (confound), and the '32% failure in another report' is traced to no listed source.
claim_before_audit: LLM-authored worked solutions and hints are less reliable than human ones: 70% passed quality checks (32% failure in another report); human hints gave significant gains and ChatGPT hints did not in v1; tutoring dialogs only 56.6% fully correct.

claim: Process-rich worked solutions (backtracking, error repair) used for fine-tuning beat clean ones: 100 examples 18.89% vs 5.56% for 1000 standard on AIME 2024 (base 6.66%). 30 problems, single run, preprint.
agent_test: Store repair traces in the library vs clean-only at equal tokens.

claim: Problem-solving-before-instruction (productive failure) is a rival: g=0.36 over 53 studies; younger learners and domain-general skills favour instruction first. Meta-analysis not read first hand.
agent_test: Compare example-first vs attempt-first-then-example on novel concept items.

claim: Worked-example gains can wash out after a delay and are mixed in primary-school and ill-structured settings.
agent_test: Test on fresh items after unrelated intervening problems.

claim: For strong instruction-tuned models, retrieved or fixed worked examples add output-format alignment but no reasoning gain at equal prompting (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct GSM8K 8-shot 95.75 vs fixed zero-shot 95.83; MATH 81.30 vs 81.64). DeepSeek-R1 reports few-shot lowers accuracy. Base models and weaker models still gain.
agent_test: Per model, run zero-shot vs one stored example with the same answer extractor; admit the example library only where it wins.

claim: Effect of a stored hint or note depends on baseline mastery of the item: pass@1 change by pre-injection per-problem accuracy was +6.31 for items at 0-50%, +2.46 at 50-100% and -2.32 at 100% (base Llama-3.2-3B); after RL the 50-100% bucket fell -5.22. Small models only, one study.
agent_test: Gate example injection on k-sample self-accuracy: hint when low, skip when the solver already agrees with itself.

claim: Subgoal-structured demonstrations beat informal-proof demonstrations when a prover checks the result: miniF2F-test minus-subgoal ablation 40.6 vs 45.5 (and 38.5 vs 44.3 without the organiser). Formal proofs, gpt-3.5, one benchmark.
agent_test: Ablate subgoal labels in library entries with a code or proof check as the outcome.

claim: In-context gains from CoT exemplars come largely from step structure and readable text, not correct numbers: wrong equations kept 24.39% vs 27.37% (PaLM-62B GSM8K), abstract symbols cost little, no-pattern prompts fall to direct level. Older models; Cheng 2026 agrees that content masking returns performance to zero-shot.
agent_test: Compare a full stored example with a format-only stub (same layout, masked content).
audit_note: Minor: the PaLM-62B finding is one older model on GSM8K; 'readable text' rests on Madaan's text ablation, which the evidence line only summarises.

claim: Answer-checked admission is not enough for example libraries: when the reference solution is shown, models copy the answer (coverage MATH 80.1 to 85.9 with masked solutions), and right-answer-wrong-reasoning solutions escape syntactic filters; no rate measured.
agent_test: Admit an example only if code reproduces the answer from a masked statement and re-derivation from the stored subgoals matches.

claim: Correct-then-store records (wrong attempt, error step, fix) used for fine-tuning beat correct-only data by 1 to 3 points (LLaMA-2-70B GSM8K 81.4 to 83.5; MATH 23.6 to 25.0). Fine-tuning, GPT-4 corrector; no in-context test of attempt-first vs example-first exists in the sources found.
agent_test: Run attempt-first-then-example vs example-first on novel items at equal tokens; this is still untested.

claim: Similarity-chosen demonstrations built from unverified self-generated chains repeat the model's own mistakes; diverse selection tolerates up to 50% wrong demos on MultiArith.
agent_test: Select library demos for diversity as well as similarity; drop chains that fail verification.
